recipes.title: Chicken Adobo
recipes.description: Chicken braised in vinegar, soy sauce, garlic and bay leaves until tender and glossy. The unofficial national dish of the Philippines.
steps: Combine the chicken, soy sauce and garlic in a pot and marinate for at least 15 minutes.
Add the water, bay leaves and peppercorns. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Pour in the vinegar and let it boil for 2 minutes without stirring to mellow the sharpness.
Lower the heat, cover and simmer for 30 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Uncover and reduce the sauce until slightly thick. Serve with steamed rice.

recipes.title: Sinigang na Baboy
recipes.description: A sour tamarind soup with tender pork belly and vegetables. Comfort food for rainy days.
steps: Boil the pork in water, skimming off the scum, then add the onion and tomatoes.
Simmer for about 1 hour until the pork is tender.
Add the radish and cook for 5 minutes, then the string beans for 3 minutes.
Stir in the tamarind soup base and season with fish sauce.
Add the kangkong, turn off the heat and serve hot.

recipes.title: Mapo Tofu
recipes.description: Silky tofu in a fiery, numbing Sichuan sauce with ground pork and fermented broad bean paste.
steps: Blanch the tofu cubes in salted simmering water for 2 minutes, then drain.
Fry the ground pork until browned, then add the doubanjiang and garlic and cook until fragrant.
Pour in the stock, slide in the tofu and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Thicken with the cornstarch slurry, pushing the tofu gently so it doesn't break.
Finish with Sichuan pepper and scallions. Serve over rice.

recipes.title: Egg Fried Rice
recipes.description: Fluffy day-old rice tossed in a hot wok with egg, scallions and soy sauce. Ready in 15 minutes.
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat until shimmering.
Pour in the eggs and scramble until just set, then break them into small pieces.
Add the rice and toss constantly for 3 to 4 minutes until every grain is hot.
Season with soy sauce and white pepper, then fold in the scallions and serve.

recipes.title: Kimchi Fried Rice
recipes.description: Tangy, spicy fried rice made with well-fermented kimchi and topped with a runny fried egg.
steps: Stir-fry the kimchi in a little oil for 3 minutes until slightly caramelized.
Add the rice, kimchi juice and gochujang and fry until evenly red and hot.
Drizzle with sesame oil and divide between two bowls.
Fry the eggs sunny side up, place one on each bowl and top with seaweed.

recipes.title: Bibimbap
recipes.description: A colorful rice bowl with seasoned vegetables, beef, a fried egg and spicy gochujang sauce, mixed together just before eating.
steps: Marinate the beef in soy sauce, sugar, garlic and sesame oil for 15 minutes.
Blanch the spinach and bean sprouts separately and season each with sesame oil and salt.
Sauté the carrot and mushrooms separately, then cook the beef over high heat.
Fry the eggs sunny side up.
Arrange everything over the rice, top with an egg and serve with gochujang to mix in.

recipes.title: Chicken Teriyaki
recipes.description: Crispy-skinned chicken thighs glazed in a sweet and savory homemade teriyaki sauce.
steps: Mix the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar into a sauce.
Place the chicken skin side down in a cold pan, then cook over medium heat for 8 minutes until crisp.
Flip and cook for another 5 minutes. Wipe out the excess fat.
Pour in the sauce and simmer, spooning it over the chicken until glossy and thick.
Slice and serve with rice, drizzling the remaining glaze on top.

recipes.title: Miso Soup
recipes.description: A light, savory soup of dashi and miso with tofu, wakame and scallions. Ready in 10 minutes.
steps: Soak the wakame in water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Heat the dashi until just below a simmer.
Dissolve the miso in a ladle of the warm dashi, then stir it back into the pot. Don't let it boil.
Add the tofu and wakame and warm through for 1 minute.
Serve topped with scallions.

ratings.comment: Lots of prep but worth it.
